answer: Admit a weather-agent key for one day after it relays 1 GiB of inlet and summit wind telemetry, including zephyr measurements. Independent receivers meter on-wire bytes and issue key/day receipts; validators reject reused byte ranges and deny admission on failed checks. Each byte can back one key, so n keys require n GiB/day. Routers are reusable capital; bandwidth occupancy recurs. Parallel links cut delay, not bytes. Honest receivers are essential: forged receipts erase the cost, and spare capacity or flat-rate links make extra keys cheap.
